scope: Engine-light locomotion mode identity (teleport, snap turn, smooth turn, continuous move), a closed typed comfort policy, locomotion intents applied to an immutable state with stable failure codes, and deterministic replay, with a thin Unity XR Interaction Toolkit locomotion-provider adapter planned separately
review_note: The URLs below were not fetched from the authoring environment because its network egress policy blocks them; the admitted claims come from the author's prior reading of these documents and must be confirmed by a person, together with the exact page paths and version pins, before the admission record is signed.

sources.license_or_terms: Unity documentation terms; architecture facts only, no XR Interaction Toolkit code copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: XR Interaction Toolkit 3.5 is the version pinned by this repository's compatibility profiles and its locomotion manual is maintained with the package; page path and version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary: the locomotion mediator, body transformer, and provider objects that the Unity adapter binds to and that the Core must not depend on
admitted_claims: Locomotion is modelled as providers that request control of the XR Origin through a mediator, which grants or denies the request so that only compatible providers move the rig at the same time
A body transformer applies queued transformations to the XR Origin in a defined order rather than each provider moving the rig directly
Teleportation, snap turn, continuous turn, and continuous move are shipped as separate provider components with their own enable state and input bindings
excluded_uses: Core does not reference LocomotionProvider, LocomotionMediator, XRBodyTransformer, XROrigin, or any other engine or toolkit type
No claim that the mediator's arbitration, transform ordering, or input reading behaves as documented without a compatibility profile and an EditMode run on that exact tuple

sources.maintenance_evidence: Shipped provider component documented in the XR Interaction Toolkit 3.5 manual; page path and version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary for the teleport mode: a teleport is a request carrying a destination and an orientation rule that the provider queues and the rig applies
admitted_claims: A teleport request carries a destination position, a destination rotation, and a match-orientation rule, and is queued on the provider rather than applied by the interactable that produced it
Teleport anchors and teleport areas are scene objects that produce requests; the provider does not know which anchor the request came from
A request is consumed once and the provider reports whether it was applied
excluded_uses: Core models a teleport as an intent to a registered anchor identity, not as a world position, and never as a scene object reference
No claim about fade, delay, or arrival behaviour on a headset without a Device Lab receipt

sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary for the snap-turn mode: a discrete rotation by a configured increment with optional turn-around
admitted_claims: Snap turn rotates the rig by a fixed configured increment per input activation, with a debounce time between turns
Left and right turns and an optional 180-degree turn-around are separate enable flags on the provider
The increment and the enable flags are serialized provider settings rather than per-input values
excluded_uses: Core owns the set of admitted increments as a comfort-policy option; the adapter writes the selected increment to the provider and never reads product tuning from the scene
No claim that a given increment is comfortable for any person or device

sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary for the smooth-turn mode: a rotation rate applied over frame time from a continuous input axis
admitted_claims: Continuous turn rotates the rig at a configured turn speed in degrees per second scaled by the input axis and the frame delta
Snap turn and continuous turn are separate providers and a project enables one or the other for a given input rather than both
Turn speed is a serialized provider setting

sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary for the continuous-move mode: a planar move vector per tick at a configured speed, with a forward source and gravity handled by the provider
admitted_claims: Continuous move translates the rig by a two-axis input scaled by a configured move speed and the frame delta, relative to a chosen forward source such as the head or a controller
Strafe, fly, and gravity are provider settings that change how the input vector is applied
Move speed is a serialized provider setting
excluded_uses: Core represents movement as an intent carrying a normalized planar vector and a tick duration, never a world-space delta computed from engine transforms
No claim about collision, ground detection, or gravity behaviour in a scene

sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary for the vignette comfort option: a field-of-view reduction driven by locomotion providers with a configurable aperture and fade
admitted_claims: A tunneling vignette controller reduces the visible field of view while a registered locomotion provider is active, then fades it back
Aperture size, feathering, ease-in and ease-out times are parameters that a provider can override while it drives the vignette
The vignette is a rendered effect attached to the camera rather than a locomotion provider
excluded_uses: Core models the vignette as a closed comfort option (enabled with an intensity range) and owns no rendering or camera type
No claim that the vignette reduces discomfort for any person or on any device
